proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate that is chemically compatible with Li-rich garnet LLZO and is a common interlayer for LiCoO2/LLZO interfaces. Its fully oxidized P5+ framework should resist oxidation at 4.0 V vs Li, so it may limit interfacial Co/La/Zr cross-reaction and space-charge formation.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, oxidation-resistant lithium zirconate with Zr4+ already present in LLZO, so the LLZO-side contact should be chemically mild and avoid the La/Zr-phosphate-type reaction seen with Li3PO4. Its Zr4+ framework should also resist oxidation against LiCoO2 at 4.0 V vs Li, which may give a lower contact penalty than Li3PO4 (0.099 eV/non-Li atom, bin 4).
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with a wide band gap, but its LLZO contact produced LaPO4 and ZrO2 with penalty 0.099 eV/non-Li atom, above the 0.05 eV threshold. This suggests an oxide whose cation chemistry is already compatible with LLZO may reduce the penalty.
